scenario: 画企业 RAG 的模型架构，面试官想听你把「检索→重排→生成」三阶段各自的优化目标讲清。
scenario_en: Sketching an enterprise RAG model architecture, the interviewer wants each of the retrieval → reranking → generation stages' objectives made clear.
q: 企业 RAG 三阶段流水线各自优化什么目标？
q_en: What objective does each stage of the enterprise RAG pipeline optimize?
why: 三阶段各优化一个不同目标：检索最大化召回(宽撒网别漏)、重排最大化精度(把最相关的排前)、生成最大化忠实度(只根据给定上下文作答别幻觉)。每阶段独立可调、有各自延迟预算，才能分别优化。
why_en: Each stage optimizes a distinct objective: retrieval maximizes recall (wide net, don't miss), reranking maximizes precision (top-rank the most relevant), and generation maximizes faithfulness (answer only from the given context, no hallucination), each independently tunable with its own latency budget.
diagram:
flowchart LR Q["查询"] --> R["检索
最大化召回 ~20ms"] --> RR["重排
最大化精度 ~50ms"] --> G["生成
最大化忠实度 ~500ms"] --> A["带引用的答案"]
options: 三阶段都优化召回，只是模型大小不同、跑得快慢不同
检索最大化召回、重排最大化精度、生成最大化忠实度，各段独立可调
检索最大化精度、重排最大化忠实度、生成最大化召回，三者对调也跑得通
三阶段其实是一个大模型端到端做，中间没法分段调优
options_en: All three optimize recall, just with different model sizes and speeds.
Retrieval maximizes recall, reranking precision, generation faithfulness — each tunable on its own.
Retrieval maximizes precision, reranking faithfulness, generation recall — swapping them works too.
It's really one big end-to-end model, so no stage can be tuned separately.
optionExplanations: 三阶段目标不同：召回、精度、忠实度各管一段，不是同一目标的三种速度。
对；分三段正是为了让召回、精度、忠实度各自独立调优，一段的旋钮不干扰另一段。
映射错了：检索管召回、重排管精度、生成管忠实度，别对调。
端到端一个模型无法分别为召回/精度/忠实度调优，也没法给每段单独的延迟预算。
optionExplanations_en: The three have different goals — recall, precision, faithfulness — not one goal at three speeds.
Correct — splitting into three lets recall, precision, and faithfulness be tuned independently without one stage's knobs disturbing another.
Mismapped: retrieval handles recall, reranking precision, generation faithfulness — don't swap them.
One end-to-end model can't tune recall/precision/faithfulness separately or give each stage its own latency budget.

termDefinitions.meaning: 生成的答案严格基于给定上下文、不编造，是生成阶段的优化目标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Faithfulness means the generated answer is grounded strictly in the given context without fabrication, the generation stage's objective.

termDefinitions.meaning: 检索增强生成：先检索文档块，再让 LLM 基于块生成有依据的答案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) retrieves chunks first, then has the LLM generate a grounded answer from them.

scenario: 面试官问三阶段各用什么模型、各占多少延迟预算，想看你对流水线的量级感。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks which model and latency budget each stage uses, checking your sense of the pipeline's magnitudes.
q: 检索/重排/生成三阶段的模型类型和延迟预算大致怎么分？
q_en: Roughly how do model type and latency budget split across retrieval/reranking/generation?
why: 检索用 bi-encoder+BM25、约 20ms；重排用 cross-encoder、约 50ms；生成用 LLM、约 500ms。延迟从检索到生成逐级放大，生成占大头，所以前两段要尽量便宜、把候选收窄后才交给昂贵的 LLM。
why_en: Retrieval uses a bi-encoder + BM25 (~20ms), reranking a cross-encoder (~50ms), generation an LLM (~500ms); latency grows down the pipeline with generation dominating, so the first two stages stay cheap and narrow candidates before the costly LLM.
tradeoff: 前段便宜快(检索/重排收窄候选) vs 生成昂贵慢(LLM 占大头延迟)
options: 三阶段延迟差不多，都在 500ms 量级，谁也不比谁贵
生成反而最快(~20ms)、重排 ~50ms、检索反而最慢(~500ms)，延迟方向说反了，其实生成才最便宜
检索 bi-encoder ~20ms、重排 cross-encoder ~50ms、生成 LLM ~500ms
三阶段都用同一个 LLM 打分和生成，延迟自然一样
options_en: All three have similar latency, around 500ms, none costlier than another.
Generation is (falsely) fastest (~20ms), reranking ~50ms, retrieval slowest (~500ms) — the direction is backwards; generation is actually the cheapest stage.
Retrieval bi-encoder ~20ms, reranking cross-encoder ~50ms, generation LLM ~500ms.
All three use the same LLM to score and generate, so latency is equal.
optionExplanations: 三阶段延迟量级差一个数量级，生成 ~500ms 远大于检索 ~20ms，不是差不多。
说反了：检索最快、生成最慢，正因如此才在生成前收窄候选。
对；便宜的检索/重排先收窄，昂贵的 LLM 只处理少量精排后的块，延迟分配才合理。
三阶段用不同模型：编码器做检索/重排、LLM 做生成，延迟量级不同。
optionExplanations_en: The stages differ by an order of magnitude — generation ~500ms far exceeds retrieval ~20ms, not similar.
Backwards: retrieval is fastest and generation slowest, which is why candidates are narrowed before generation.
Correct — cheap retrieval/reranking narrow first so the costly LLM handles only a few reranked chunks, a sensible latency split.
The stages use different models — encoders for retrieval/reranking, an LLM for generation — with different latency magnitudes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分别把查询和文档编码成向量再比距离，快但不建模两者交互。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A bi-encoder encodes query and document into vectors separately then compares distance — fast but models no interaction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把查询和文档拼在一起送入 transformer 联合打分，精但慢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cross-encoder feeds the query and document jointly through a transformer for a joint score — precise but slow.

scenario: 检索为了召回把网撒得很宽，一次拉回 20-50 个候选块，但 LLM 上下文实际只放得下 5-10 个。
scenario_en: Retrieval casts a wide net for recall, pulling 20-50 candidate chunks, but the LLM context only holds 5-10.
q: 为什么在检索和生成之间还要插一个重排阶段？
q_en: Why insert a reranking stage between retrieval and generation?
why: 检索为召回撒宽网(20-50 块)，但上下文只放得下 5-10 块，必须有人把这一大堆里真正最相关的挑到前面。重排就是这个精度过滤器：把宽候选集变成精排短名单，让塞进上下文的都是最相关的。
why_en: Retrieval casts a wide net for recall (20-50 chunks) but the context fits only 5-10, so something must pick the truly most relevant to the top — reranking is that precision filter, turning the broad set into a precise shortlist so only the most relevant enter the context.
options: 重排是精度过滤器：把 20-50 的宽候选精排成 5-10 的短名单
重排把检索结果随机打乱来增加多样性，避免同源块扎堆
重排负责把候选块翻译成统一语言，方便模型阅读理解
重排是可选的，直接把检索出的 20-50 块原样塞进上下文，图省事最快
options_en: Reranking is a precision filter: it condenses 20-50 broad candidates into a 5-10 shortlist.
Reranking randomly shuffles retrieval results for diversity so same-source chunks do not clump.
Reranking translates candidate chunks into one common language so the model reads them easily.
Reranking is optional — just dump all 20-50 retrieved chunks into the context as-is, fastest and simplest.
optionExplanations: 对；召回宽但上下文窄，重排负责在两者之间把最相关的精排到前列，是让上下文装配可行的关键。
打乱只会破坏相关性排序，与重排要提升精度的目标相反。
翻译不是重排的职责，重排是按相关性给候选打分排序。
20-50 块塞不进只放 5-10 的上下文，且会引入大量噪声块，必须重排收窄。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — recall is wide but context narrow, so reranking picks the most relevant to the top between them, making context assembly feasible.
Shuffling destroys the relevance order, opposite to reranking's precision goal.
Translation isn't reranking's job; reranking scores and orders candidates by relevance.
20-50 chunks won't fit a 5-10 context and add noise chunks, so reranking must narrow them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在检索召回的候选集里按相关性精排，选出最相关的少数进上下文。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Reranking re-orders the retrieved candidate set by relevance to pick the few most relevant for the context.

scenario: 重排要在少量候选块上追求最高相关性精度，愿意为此付更高的单次计算成本。
scenario_en: Reranking wants top relevance precision on a few candidate chunks and will pay a higher per-item compute cost for it.
q: 重排阶段该用 cross-encoder 还是 bi-encoder，为什么？
q_en: Should reranking use a cross-encoder or a bi-encoder, and why?
why: 用 cross-encoder：查询和块拼一起联合打分，能捕捉 bi-encoder 独立编码时看不到的细粒度交互。代价是每对都要现算、O(n) 慢，只在少量候选上跑。
why_en: Use a cross-encoder: it feeds the query and each chunk jointly through a transformer to capture query-document interactions a bi-encoder misses (bi-encoders encode each independently then compare vectors), giving higher precision, at O(n) cost so it only runs on few candidates.
tradeoff: cross-encoder(联合打分精度高但 O(n) 慢) vs bi-encoder(独立编码快但漏交互)
whenOtherWins: 第一阶段海量检索(在整个索引上打分)必须用 bi-encoder，因为可预计算文档向量、毫秒级 ANN，cross-encoder 在那个规模上跑不动。
options: 用 bi-encoder，独立编码查询和块再比向量，最快所以最适合重排，精度也够用
用 cross-encoder：查询和块拼一起联合打分，精度高但只跑少量候选
重排不需要模型，直接复用检索阶段的相似度分数就行
用一个大 LLM 给每个块写摘要，按摘要长度当重排分数
options_en: Use a bi-encoder: encode query and chunk separately, compare vectors — fastest, so best for reranking, and precise enough.
Use a cross-encoder: score query and chunk jointly — high precision, but run it on few candidates only.
Reranking needs no model; just reuse the similarity scores from the retrieval stage.
Have a big LLM summarize each chunk and use summary length as the rerank score.
optionExplanations: bi-encoder 快是因为独立编码、不建模交互，正因如此精度不如 cross-encoder，做不好重排的精排。
对；联合打分让模型看到查询和块的细粒度交互，精度高；候选已被收窄到 20-50，O(n) 成本可承受。
直接复用检索分数就等于没重排，检索的召回分不足以做精度排序。
让 LLM 逐块摘要又慢又贵，还不如 cross-encoder 直接给相关性分。
optionExplanations_en: A bi-encoder is fast because it encodes independently without modeling interaction, so it's less precise and poor at fine reranking.
Correct — joint scoring lets the model see fine query-chunk interactions for high precision, and with candidates narrowed to 20-50 the O(n) cost is affordable.
Reusing retrieval scores is no reranking; recall-oriented scores don't give precise ordering.
Summarizing each chunk with an LLM is slow and costly, worse than a cross-encoder's direct relevance score.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把查询和文档拼接送入 transformer 联合打分，捕捉两者交互，精但 O(n)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cross-encoder concatenates query and document into a transformer for a joint score, capturing interaction — precise but O(n).

termDefinitions.fullName: BERT = Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers
termDefinitions.meaning: 常见的 cross-encoder 重排器基于微调的 BERT(如 bge-reranker)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Common cross-encoder rerankers are fine-tuned BERT (Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers) models such as bge-reranker.

scenario: 面试官要你讲清 cross-encoder 和 bi-encoder 的机制差别，以及为什么两阶段各用一个。
scenario_en: The interviewer wants the mechanism difference between cross- and bi-encoders and why each stage uses one.
q: cross-encoder 和 bi-encoder 在编码方式、速度、精度上如何对比？
q_en: How do cross- and bi-encoders contrast on encoding, speed, and precision?
why: bi-encoder 各自独立编码、可预计算文档向量，比向量毫秒级但漏细交互；cross-encoder 拼一起联合过 transformer，精度高但每对现算、O(n) 慢。
why_en: A bi-encoder encodes query and document separately with precomputable doc vectors, so retrieval compares vectors in milliseconds — fast but missing fine interaction; a cross-encoder feeds them jointly through a transformer, seeing interactions for high precision but computing each pair live at O(n), so retrieval uses bi-encoders and reranking cross-encoders.
tradeoff: bi-encoder(独立编码、可预算、快但漏交互) vs cross-encoder(联合打分、精但每对现算、慢)
options: 两者机制其实差不多，只是叫法不同，速度和精度没有本质差别
cross-encoder 独立编码更快、bi-encoder 联合打分更慢，这个说法正好反了
bi-encoder 独立编码可预计算但漏交互；cross-encoder 联合打分精度高但慢
两者都必须实时联合打分，谁都无法把文档向量预先算好
options_en: The two are basically the same mechanism, just different names, with no real speed or precision gap.
Cross-encoders encode independently and are faster, bi-encoders score jointly and are slower — that claim is exactly backwards.
Bi-encoder encodes independently and is precomputable but misses interaction; cross-encoder scores jointly for high precision but is slow.
Both must score jointly in real time — neither can precompute document vectors.
optionExplanations: 错——两者机制根本不同：独立编码 vs 联合打分，正是它拉开了速度和精度差距，绝非只换了个名字。
说反了：bi-encoder 独立编码更快、cross-encoder 联合打分更慢。
对；这正解释了为什么海量检索用可预计算的前者、少量重排才用得起精度更高的后者。
bi-encoder 恰恰能预计算文档向量，说都不能预计算是错的。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong — the mechanisms differ fundamentally: independent encoding vs joint scoring is exactly what drives the speed and precision gap, not a mere renaming.
Backwards: bi-encoders encode independently and are faster, cross-encoders score jointly and are slower.
Correct — that is exactly why massive retrieval uses the cheaper former (precompute once) while only small-scale reranking can afford the costlier latter (compute per pair).
Bi-encoders can precompute doc vectors, so saying neither can precompute is wrong.

termDefinitions.meaning: 计算量随候选数 n 线性增长；cross-encoder 每个候选都要单独过一次模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: O(n) means cost grows linearly with the candidate count n; a cross-encoder runs the model once per candidate.

scenario: cross-encoder 重排的计算量随候选数 O(n) 线性增长，而重排阶段的延迟预算约 50ms。
scenario_en: Cross-encoder reranking cost grows O(n) with candidate count, and the reranking budget is ~50ms.
q: 「cross-encoder 是 O(n)、预算 ~50ms」这组约束在设计里怎么用？
q_en: How do you use the 'cross-encoder O(n), ~50ms budget' constraints in design?
why: 因为 O(n)：候选越多重排越慢，要把送进重排的候选数封顶在 20-50 才能压进 ~50ms 预算。这不是背数字，而是「复杂度×预算」定出候选上限——检索召回可以宽，但交给重排前必须先截到这个量级。
why_en: Because it's O(n), more candidates mean slower reranking, so cap the candidates entering reranking at 20-50 to fit the ~50ms budget — not a number to memorize but complexity × budget setting the cap: retrieval can recall wide, but must be trimmed to this magnitude before reranking.
options: 候选封顶 20-50：O(n) 下越多越慢，才压得进 ~50ms 预算
候选越多越好，直接把检索到的几千个候选块全部塞进重排流程里跑
50ms 就是要死记硬背的数字，考点单纯是记住这个 50
O(n) 说明重排耗时和候选数量完全无关，随便塞多少块进去速度都一样快
options_en: Cap candidates at 20-50: under O(n) more candidates means slower, and only that cap fits the ~50ms budget.
More candidates are always better; send all the thousands from retrieval straight into reranking.
50ms is just a number to memorize by rote; the point is recalling this 50.
O(n) means reranking time has nothing to do with candidate count at all, so any number of candidates runs equally fast.

termDefinitions.meaning: 送进重排的候选块数量上限，由 cross-encoder 的 O(n) 成本和延迟预算共同决定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The candidate cap is the max chunks entering reranking, set jointly by the cross-encoder's O(n) cost and the latency budget.

optionExplanations: 对，这就是把复杂度和预算换算成候选数量级的做法。
误解：塞得越多重排跑得越慢，几千个候选会直接击穿 ~50ms 的延迟预算。
误解：50 不是要背的数字，它是复杂度和预算共同推出来的候选上限。
误解：O(n) 恰恰说明候选数越多耗时越长，不是无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — it converts complexity and the latency budget into a candidate-count ceiling.
Misconception: more candidates make reranking slower, and thousands of them would blow through the ~50ms budget.
Misconception: 50 is not a number to memorize; it's the candidate cap derived from complexity times budget.
Misconception: O(n) means the opposite — more candidates cost more time, not the same speed.

scenario: 通用重排器在法务/医疗语料上分不清「相关」和「看着相关但其实不对」的块，精度不够。
scenario_en: A generic reranker can't tell relevant from look-relevant-but-wrong chunks on legal/medical corpora, so precision is low.
q: 重排精度在专业领域不够，最有效的提升手段是什么？
q_en: What most effectively improves reranking precision in a specialized domain?
why: 在领域相关性判断(query-chunk 是否真相关的人工标注)上微调重排器：让它学会本领域「什么才算真相关」，精度提升很大。通用重排器没见过领域判据，分不清近似相关和真正相关。
why_en: Fine-tune the reranker on domain relevance judgments (human labels of whether a query-chunk pair is truly relevant): it learns what counts as relevant in this domain for a big precision gain, whereas a generic reranker hasn't seen domain criteria and confuses near-relevant with truly relevant.
tradeoff: 领域微调重排器(精度大涨但要标注判断) vs 通用重排器(零成本但领域精度不足)
whenOtherWins: 若语料是通用日常文本、没有专业相关性判据，现成通用重排器已够，微调是多余成本。
options: 把候选数从 20 提到 200，让重排看到更多可能相关的块
换更大的生成 LLM，让它在生成阶段自行纠正相关性错误
在领域相关性标注上微调重排器，学会本领域什么算真相关
关掉重排，直接用检索的向量相似度分数排序
options_en: Raise candidates from 20 to 200 so the reranker sees more possibly relevant chunks.
Switch to a bigger generation LLM and let it fix relevance mistakes while generating.
Fine-tune the reranker on domain relevance labels so it learns what truly counts as relevant here.
Turn reranking off and just order by retrieval vector similarity.
optionExplanations: 加候选数只会撑爆 O(n) 延迟预算，不解决「分不清真相关」这个精度问题。
生成 LLM 只能用重排后给它的块，重排排错了 LLM 补不回来。
对；用领域标注微调让重排器习得本领域的相关性判据，是提升领域精度最直接的手段。
用检索分数排序等于放弃精度过滤，专业领域的近似相关块会大量混入。
optionExplanations_en: More candidates only blow the O(n) budget and don't fix the precision problem of confusing true relevance.
The generation LLM can only use the chunks reranking gave it; if reranking mis-ordered, it can't recover.
Correct — domain-labeled fine-tuning teaches the reranker this domain's relevance criteria, the most direct precision fix.
Ordering by retrieval score abandons the precision filter, letting many near-relevant chunks in on specialized domains.

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工标注某查询-文档块对是否真正相关，用来微调重排器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A relevance judgment is a human label of whether a query-chunk pair is truly relevant, used to fine-tune a reranker.

scenario: 一个 8K 上下文窗口，并不是有 8K token 全给检索到的文档块用。
scenario_en: An 8K context window is not 8K tokens all available for the retrieved chunks.
q: 检索块真正可用的「token 预算」怎么算？
q_en: How is the actual 'token budget' for retrieved chunks computed?
why: token 预算 = 窗口大小 − 系统提示 − few-shot 示例 − 为输出预留的 token。8K 窗口扣掉这些后剩下的才是能塞文档块的额度，所以规划上下文不能按窗口全长算。
why_en: Token budget = window size − system prompt − few-shot examples − output reservation; only what remains after subtracting these from the 8K window can hold chunks, so you can't plan context by the full window length.
options: token 预算 = 窗口全长，8K 窗口就是 8K 全部拿来放检索到的文档块
token 预算 = 窗口 − 系统提示 − few-shot 示例 − 输出预留
token 预算 = 窗口 × 2，因为输入和输出各算一遍额度
token 预算只由检索到的块数量决定，与系统提示和输出预留无关
options_en: Token budget = the full window; an 8K window means all 8K goes to the retrieved chunks.
Token budget = window − system prompt − few-shot examples − output reservation.
Token budget = window × 2, since input and output each get counted.
Token budget depends only on how many chunks were retrieved, not on the system prompt or output reservation.
optionExplanations: 系统提示、few-shot、输出都占窗口，按全长算会溢出，真正给块的没那么多。
对；先扣掉固定开销和输出预留，剩下的才是块的额度，这是上下文装配的第一步。
窗口是输入输出共享的总额度，不能翻倍，输出还要预留占用。
系统提示等固定开销直接吃掉窗口，预算当然和它有关。
optionExplanations_en: System prompt, few-shot, and output all occupy the window, so counting the full length overflows; chunks get much less.
Correct — subtract fixed overhead and output reservation first; the remainder is the chunk budget, the first step of context assembly.
The window is a shared input+output total, not doubled, and output must be reserved.
Fixed overhead like the system prompt eats the window, so the budget does depend on it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 上下文窗口扣掉系统提示、few-shot、输出预留后，剩给文档块的 token 额度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The token budget is the window minus the system prompt, few-shot, and output reservation — the tokens left for chunks.

termDefinitions.meaning: 放进提示里的几条示范样例，引导 LLM 的输出格式或行为，占用窗口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Few-shot examples are demonstration samples placed in the prompt to steer the LLM's format or behavior, occupying the window.

scenario: 重排后的候选块加起来超过了 token 预算，你要决定放哪些、溢出的那块怎么处理。
scenario_en: The reranked chunks together exceed the token budget, and you must decide which to include and how to handle the overflow.
q: 上下文装配的基础做法是什么？
q_en: What is the baseline approach to context assembly?
why: 贪心选择+截断：按重排分从高到低依次加块，直到预算用尽；对刚好溢出的那一块，在句子边界处截断(而不是切在 token 中间)，保住语义连贯。这是简单可靠的基线。
why_en: Greedy selection + truncation: add chunks in descending rerank-score order until the budget is exhausted, then truncate the overflowing chunk at a sentence boundary (not mid-token) to keep coherence — a simple, reliable baseline.
tradeoff: 贪心+句界截断(简单可靠但可能砍掉低分块细节) vs 相关性加权分配(更细但更复杂)
whenOtherWins: 若各块相关性差异很大、想让高分块拿更多篇幅、低分块被摘要而非硬截，就升级到相关性加权分配。
options: 把所有检索到的块都原样硬塞进去，超出预算也完全不管
按重排分从高到低加块直到预算用尽，溢出块在句子边界截断
随机挑几块放进去，反正 LLM 自己能理解上下文
只放分最低的块，把高分块留给后续追问时再用
options_en: Cram in every retrieved chunk as-is, completely ignoring the budget overflow.
Add chunks by descending rerank score until the budget runs out, truncating the overflow at a sentence boundary.
Pick a few chunks at random — the LLM will figure out the context anyway.
Include only the lowest-scored chunks and save the top ones for follow-up turns.
optionExplanations: 硬塞超预算会被模型截断或报错，且截在哪不可控，容易砍掉关键内容。
对；按分贪心装配 + 句界截断，既优先放最相关的、又避免把一句话切碎，是可靠基线。
随机挑放弃了相关性排序，把重排的成果浪费掉。
只放低分块本末倒置，最相关的高分块反而进不去。
optionExplanations_en: Cramming over budget gets truncated or errors, with an uncontrolled cut point that may drop key content.
Correct — greedy assembly by score plus sentence-boundary truncation prioritizes the most relevant while avoiding cutting a sentence apart, a reliable baseline.
Random picks abandon the relevance order, wasting the reranking work.
Including only low-scored chunks is backwards; the most relevant high-scored chunks would be excluded.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把溢出的块在句号等句子边界处切断，而非切在 token 中间，保语义连贯。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sentence-boundary truncation cuts an overflowing chunk at a sentence end rather than mid-token, preserving coherence.

scenario: 候选块相关性差异很大：头部两块高度相关、后面几块只是勉强相关，token 预算又有限。
scenario_en: Candidate chunks vary widely in relevance: the top two are highly relevant, the rest only marginally, and the token budget is tight.
q: 比贪心截断更精细的上下文分配怎么做？
q_en: What is a more refined context allocation than greedy truncation?
why: 用相关性加权分配：分越高的块分到越多 token 预算(完整保留)，分低的块被摘要压缩或直接丢弃，而不是一刀切均分。这样把有限预算集中在最相关内容上，比贪心+硬截更省 token、信息密度更高。
why_en: Use relevance-weighted allocation: higher-scored chunks get more of the token budget (kept in full) while lower ones are summarized or dropped, rather than a flat split, concentrating the limited budget on the most relevant content for higher information density than greedy hard truncation.
tradeoff: 相关性加权分配(高分块给更多篇幅、低分摘要/丢弃但更复杂) vs 贪心均等(简单但浪费在低分块上)
whenOtherWins: 若各块相关性接近、预算也够，贪心+句界截断更简单，没必要上摘要和加权的复杂度。
options: 不管分数高低，每块分同样多的 token，公平均分
相关性加权分配：高分块给更多预算，低分块摘要或丢弃
把所有块都先摘要成一句话再放进上下文
只按块的原始长度分配，长的块给更多预算
options_en: Ignore scores and give every chunk the same number of tokens, an even split.
Relevance-weighted allocation: high-scored chunks get more budget, low-scored ones are summarized or dropped.
Summarize every chunk down to one sentence before putting it in the context.
Allocate purely by original chunk length; longer chunks get more budget.
optionExplanations: 均分把预算浪费在勉强相关的块上，挤掉了高分块本该完整保留的内容。
对；按相关性把预算倾斜给高分块、压缩或丢弃低分块，让有限上下文信息密度最高。
把高分块也摘要成一句会丢关键细节，忠实度反而下降。
按长度分配与相关性无关，可能给一个又长又不相关的块最多篇幅。
optionExplanations_en: An equal split wastes budget on marginally relevant chunks and squeezes out content the high-scored chunks should keep in full.
Correct — skewing budget toward high-scored chunks and compressing/dropping low ones maximizes information density in limited context.
Summarizing even high-scored chunks to one sentence loses key detail, lowering faithfulness.
Allocating by length ignores relevance and may give a long, irrelevant chunk the most room.

termDefinitions.term: relevance-weighted allocation / 相关性加权分配
termDefinitions.meaning: 按重排分把 token 预算倾斜给高分块，低分块摘要或丢弃。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Relevance-weighted allocation skews the token budget toward high-scored chunks and summarizes or drops low ones.

scenario: 你把最相关的块随手放在了一长串上下文的正中间，前后堆着不太相关的块。
scenario_en: You place the most relevant chunk right in the middle of a long context, padded before and after with less relevant chunks.
q: 「lost-in-the-middle」效应会导致什么，根因是什么？
q_en: What does the lost-in-the-middle effect cause, and why?
why: LLM 更充分利用上下文开头和结尾的信息，中间的相对被忽略。把最相关的块埋在中间→模型对它关注不足→即使检索/重排都对，答案仍可能漏掉这条关键证据。所以要按位置感知排序，把最相关的放首尾。
why_en: LLMs use information at the beginning and end of the context more than the middle, so burying the most relevant chunk in the middle gets it under-attended and the answer may miss that key evidence even though retrieval and reranking were correct — hence position-aware ordering puts the most relevant first and last.
diagram:
flowchart LR B["开头
高关注"] --> M["中间
低关注"] --> E["结尾
高关注"]
options: 没有影响，LLM 对上下文各个位置一视同仁
LLM 更关注首尾、忽略中间，最相关块埋中间会被漏掉
只会让生成变慢，是纯粹的性能问题，不影响正确性
会让 LLM 更关注中间，所以最相关的块就该放中间
options_en: No effect — the LLM treats every context position equally.
The LLM attends to the start and end and neglects the middle, so a top chunk buried there gets missed.
It only slows generation down — a pure performance issue, not a correctness one.
It makes the LLM focus on the middle, so the most relevant chunk belongs there.
optionExplanations: 实证上 LLM 对首尾利用明显强于中间，位置并非一视同仁。
对；这正是 lost-in-the-middle：把最相关的埋中间会被忽略，修法是把它放首尾。
这是关注度问题不是速度问题，影响的是答案质量而非延迟。
说反了：中间是被忽略的区域，最相关的恰恰不该放中间。
optionExplanations_en: Empirically the LLM uses the start and end far more than the middle, so positions aren't equal.
Correct — this is lost-in-the-middle: burying the top chunk in the middle gets it ignored, fixed by placing it at the ends.
It's an attention issue not speed, affecting answer quality not latency.
Backwards: the middle is the neglected region, so the most relevant chunk should not go there.

termDefinitions.meaning: LLM 对上下文首尾信息利用强、对中间信息利用弱的现象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Lost-in-the-middle is the phenomenon that LLMs use context at the start and end more than in the middle.

scenario: 已知 LLM 对上下文首尾利用更强、中间更弱，你要安排 5 个重排后块的摆放顺序。
scenario_en: Knowing LLMs use the start and end more than the middle, you must order 5 reranked chunks in the context.
q: 怎么摆放块的顺序来对抗 lost-in-the-middle？
q_en: How do you order chunks to counter lost-in-the-middle?
why: 用位置感知排序：把最相关的块放在开头和结尾这两个高关注位置，把相对次要的放中间。这样即便存在中间迷失，最关键的证据仍落在模型最能利用的位置上。
why_en: Use position-aware ordering: put the most relevant chunks at the start and end (the high-attention positions) and less relevant ones in the middle, so even with lost-in-the-middle the key evidence sits where the model uses it best.
tradeoff: 位置感知排序(把最相关放首尾、对抗中间迷失) vs 纯按分顺序堆(简单但最相关可能落中间)
whenOtherWins: 若上下文很短(只有 2-3 块)、根本没有「中间」可言，纯按分顺序放就够，位置技巧收益不大。
options: 按重排分从高到低顺序堆，最相关的自然排第一，后面递减
把最相关的块放开头和结尾这两个高关注位，次要的放中间
把最相关的放正中间，因为那里最显眼
随机打乱顺序，避免模型形成位置偏好
options_en: Stack in descending rerank score; the most relevant is first, then decreasing.
Put the most relevant chunks at the start and end (high-attention positions), less relevant in the middle.
Put the most relevant in the dead center since it's most prominent.
Shuffle randomly to keep the model from forming a position bias.
optionExplanations: 纯降序会把第二、第三相关的块推到中间的被忽略区，浪费它们的价值。
对；把最相关的放首尾正好落在模型最能利用的位置，是对抗中间迷失的直接做法。
正中间恰恰是被忽略的区域，把最相关放那里适得其反。
随机打乱既不利用首尾优势，也可能把最关键证据丢进中间。
optionExplanations_en: Pure descending order pushes the 2nd/3rd most relevant into the neglected middle, wasting their value.
Correct — placing the most relevant at the ends lands them where the model uses them best, the direct counter to lost-in-the-middle.
The dead center is the neglected region, so putting the most relevant there backfires.
Random shuffling neither exploits the ends nor prevents key evidence landing in the middle.

termDefinitions.term: position-aware ordering / 位置感知排序
termDefinitions.meaning: 按 LLM 对首尾关注更强的特点，把最相关块放到开头和结尾。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Position-aware ordering places the most relevant chunks at the start and end, exploiting the LLM's stronger attention there.

scenario: 有人提议：把上下文窗口从 8K 换成 128K，把更多块一股脑塞进去，答案就会更好。
scenario_en: Someone proposes swapping the 8K window for 128K and dumping in far more chunks to get better answers.
q: 「窗口越大、塞越多块，答案一定越好」这个想法对吗？
q_en: Is 'a bigger window with more chunks always gives better answers' correct?
why: 不对。更大窗口≠更好答案：块越多噪声越多、关键证据更容易落进被忽略的中间(lost-in-the-middle)，还更慢更贵。正解仍是重排收窄+位置感知排序，把少而精的块放对位置，而非无脑塞满。
why_en: No — a bigger window doesn't mean better answers: more chunks add noise, key evidence is more likely buried in the neglected middle (lost-in-the-middle), and it's slower and costlier; the fix is still reranking to narrow plus position-aware ordering, not stuffing.
options: 对，窗口越大能塞越多块，信息越全答案就越好
不对：块越多噪声越多，关键证据更易落进被忽略的中间
对，只要塞满窗口就不用重排和位置排序了
不对，因为大窗口会让模型直接崩溃，根本无法生成
options_en: Yes — a bigger window holds more chunks, and more complete info gives better answers.
No: more chunks mean more noise, and key evidence more easily lands in the neglected middle.
Yes — once you fill the window you can skip reranking and position ordering.
No, because a large window makes the model crash and it cannot generate at all.
optionExplanations: 更全不等于更好：无关块会稀释注意力，关键证据被埋，答案质量反而下降。
对；大窗口引入噪声和中间迷失、又慢又贵，正解是收窄+摆对位置而非塞满。
塞满不做重排会把大量噪声块喂给模型，正是要避免的做法。
大窗口不会让模型崩溃，问题是注意力稀释和中间迷失，不是无法生成。
optionExplanations_en: More complete isn't better: irrelevant chunks dilute attention and bury key evidence, lowering quality.
Correct — a big window adds noise and lost-in-the-middle and is slow and costly, so narrow and position well rather than stuff.
Stuffing without reranking feeds many noise chunks to the model, exactly what to avoid.
A big window doesn't crash the model; the issue is attention dilution and lost-in-the-middle, not inability to generate.

termDefinitions.meaning: LLM 单次能读入的最大 token 数；更大不自动带来更好答案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The context window is the max tokens an LLM reads at once; larger doesn't automatically yield better answers.

scenario: 上下文窗口 4096 token，其中 800 留给系统提示+few-shot+输出；重排后候选块按分从高到低是 900/800/700/600/500 token。
scenario_en: A 4096-token window with 800 reserved for prompt+output; reranked chunks by score are 900/800/700/600/500 tokens.
q: 这个窗口能放下几个块，第 5 个怎么处理？
q_en: How many chunks fit, and what happens to the 5th?
why_en: Token budget = 4096 − 800 = 3296; greedily add by score: 900+800+700+600 = 3000 (296 left), the 5th (500) doesn't fit → truncate it at a sentence boundary within the remaining 296, demonstrating budget = window − overhead then greedy assembly.
options: 5 个块全放得下，因为 4096 这个总长度足够装下全部块，不用管开销
只放得下 2 个块，把 900 和 800 加起来凑够就直接放弃后面剩下的全部块
预算 3296：前 4 个共 3000 放下，第 5 个超出，在剩余 296 内截断
预算按 4096 全长算，5 个块全放，最后一个也不用截断
options_en: All 5 fit, because the 4096 total length is enough for every chunk, no need to account for overhead.
Only 2 fit; once 900 and 800 add up, drop everything else that remains outright.
Budget 3296: the first 4 totaling 3000 fit, the 5th overflows, truncated within the remaining 296.
Budget uses the full 4096 length; all 5 fit and the last needs no truncation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按分从高到低依次加块直到预算用尽的装配策略。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Greedy selection adds chunks in descending score until the budget is exhausted.

optionExplanations: 误解：4096 是窗口全长，没扣掉 800 的开销，实际能用的只有 3296。
误解：只算了前两个块就放弃，其实 3296 预算够装下前 4 个块。
对，先扣开销得 3296，再按分贪心装，第 5 个超出后在剩余空间内截断。
误解：预算不是窗口全长，4096 里有 800 要扣掉，装不下全部 5 个。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: 4096 is the full window; without subtracting the 800 overhead, only 3296 is actually usable.
Misconception: stopping after only two chunks is wrong — the 3296 budget actually fits the first 4.
Correct — subtract overhead to get 3296, greedily add by score, and truncate the 5th within what's left.
Misconception: the budget is not the full window; 4096 minus the 800 overhead means all 5 do not fit.

scenario: 企业合规要求 RAG 不泄露 PII、不越权、不幻觉、不输出有害内容，单一防护措施不够。
scenario_en: Enterprise compliance requires the RAG to not leak PII, not exceed permissions, not hallucinate, and not output harmful content — one guardrail isn't enough.
q: 企业 RAG 的护栏为什么要分三层，怎么对应流水线位置？
q_en: Why are enterprise RAG guardrails in three layers, and how do they map to pipeline position?
why: 护栏按流水线位置分三层做纵深防御：生成前(块进 prompt 前做 PII 脱敏、权限过滤)、prompt 级(下 grounding 指令、强制引用)、生成后(核验引用、内容安全、幻觉检测)。任一层都不足以单独兜住合规，分层各挡一类风险。
why_en: Guardrails split into three layers by pipeline position for defense-in-depth: pre-generation (PII redaction and permission filtering before chunks enter the prompt), prompt-level (grounding instructions, citation enforcement), and post-generation (citation verification, content safety, hallucination detection) — no single layer suffices, so each blocks a class of risk.

flowchart LR Pre["生成前
PII脱敏/权限过滤"] --> Prm["prompt级
grounding/强制引用"] --> Post["生成后
引用核验/安全/幻觉检测"]
options: 护栏只需一层放在生成后就够，前面各阶段不用管
按流水线位置分三层：生成前/prompt 级/生成后，纵深防御
三层护栏干脆都堆在生成这一层之后，同一套安全检查重复三遍更保险
护栏和流水线位置无关，放在哪一层效果都一样
options_en: One guardrail layer after generation is enough; earlier stages need none.
Three layers by pipeline position — pre-generation, prompt level, post-generation — for defense in depth.
Just stack all three layers after the generation stage, repeating the same safety check three times to be safer.
Guardrails have nothing to do with pipeline position; any layer works the same.
optionExplanations: 只在生成后拦，PII 早已进了 prompt、越权块早已被读，泄露已发生，拦不住。
对；每层挡不同风险——生成前防泄露、prompt 级促忠实、生成后查幻觉，分层才覆盖全。
三层都堆生成后无法阻止生成前的泄露和越权，位置错了重复也没用。
位置决定能挡住哪类风险，PII 必须生成前挡、幻觉必须生成后查，不能随意。
optionExplanations_en: Blocking only after generation is too late — PII already entered the prompt and unauthorized chunks were already read, so the leak already happened.
Correct — each layer blocks a different risk: pre-gen prevents leakage, prompt-level drives faithfulness, post-gen catches hallucination, so layering covers all.
Stacking all three after generation can't stop pre-generation leakage or over-permission; repetition in the wrong place doesn't help.
Position decides which risk you can block — PII must be caught pre-gen and hallucination post-gen — so it can't be arbitrary.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在 RAG 流水线不同位置加的安全/合规检查，纵深防御防泄露、越权、幻觉、有害输出。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Guardrails are safety/compliance checks at different pipeline points, a defense-in-depth against leakage, over-permission, hallucination, and harmful output.

termDefinitions.meaning: 个人可识别信息(如身份证号、邮箱、电话)，合规要求在进 prompt 前脱敏。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PII (Personally Identifiable Information) like SSNs, emails, and phones must be redacted before entering the prompt for compliance.

scenario: 生成前这一层要在文档块进入 prompt 之前，先挡住会造成泄露或越权的风险。
scenario_en: The pre-generation layer must block leakage and over-permission risks before chunks enter the prompt.
q: 生成前(pre-generation)护栏包含哪些措施？(多选)
q_en: Which measures make up pre-generation guardrails? (multiple)
why: 生成前三招都在块进 prompt 之前动手：PII 脱敏(NER/正则抓证件、邮箱)、基于 ACL 的权限过滤、块相关性阈值过滤。生成后核验是另一层。
why_en: All three act before chunks enter the prompt: PII detection and redaction (NER or regex for SSN/email/phone, for GDPR/HIPAA), ACL-based permission filtering (drop chunks the user may not see), and a chunk relevance threshold (weak chunks below it don't enter). Citation verification belongs to a later layer.
options: PII 检测与脱敏(NER/正则抓身份证/邮箱/电话)，防个人信息进 prompt
基于 ACL 的权限过滤，剔掉用户无权访问的块
块相关性阈值，低于阈值的弱相关块不进 prompt
生成后核验每条引用是否真被块支持
options_en: PII detection and redaction (NER/regex for SSN/email/phone) to keep PII out of the prompt.
ACL-based permission filtering to drop chunks the user can't access.
A chunk relevance threshold so weakly relevant chunks don't enter the prompt.
Post-generation verification that each citation is actually supported by the chunk.
optionExplanations: 对；PII 脱敏挡住个人信息在进 prompt 前就外泄，满足 GDPR/HIPAA 合规。
对；权限过滤挡住越权泄露——用户无权看的块根本不进上下文。
对；相关性阈值挡住噪声块，减少无关内容稀释注意力和引发幻觉的压力。
错；引用核验发生在生成之后，属于生成后层，不是生成前措施。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — PII redaction blocks personal info from leaking before it enters the prompt, meeting GDPR/HIPAA.
Correct — permission filtering blocks over-permission leakage: chunks the user can't see never enter context.
Correct — a relevance threshold blocks noise chunks, reducing attention dilution and hallucination pressure.
Incorrect — citation verification happens after generation, in the post-gen layer, not a pre-gen measure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 命名实体识别，用来在文本中定位姓名/身份证/邮箱等 PII 以便脱敏。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NER (Named Entity Recognition) locates entities like names, SSNs, and emails in text so PII can be redacted.

termDefinitions.meaning: 访问控制列表，规定谁能看哪些块，生成前据此过滤越权内容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ACL (Access Control List) specifies who may see which chunks, used pre-generation to filter unauthorized content.

scenario: 要让 RAG 只根据检索到的块作答、每条结论都能追溯到来源，减少编造。
scenario_en: You want the RAG to answer only from retrieved chunks and make each claim traceable to a source, reducing fabrication.
q: prompt 级护栏靠什么约束模型的生成行为？
q_en: What does the prompt-level guardrail use to constrain generation?
why: 用 grounding 指令：在 prompt 里明确要求「只根据提供的上下文作答、每条结论标注引用的 chunk ID」，并放几个「上下文不足就拒答」的 few-shot 示例。这把忠实度和可追溯性写进指令，减少幻觉。
why_en: Use grounding instructions: the prompt explicitly says 'answer only from the provided context and cite the chunk ID for each claim,' plus a few few-shot refusal examples ('refuse when context is insufficient'), baking faithfulness and traceability into the instructions to cut hallucination.
tradeoff: grounding 指令(强忠实/可追溯但可能过度拒答) vs 自由生成(流畅但易幻觉、不可追溯)
whenOtherWins: 若任务是开放式头脑风暴、本就期望模型发挥而非严格引用，过强的 grounding 指令反而限制有用输出。
options: 完全不给约束指令，让模型凭自己的知识自由发挥最自然
grounding 指令：只按上下文作答、结论标 chunk ID
在指令里要求模型尽量多补充上下文之外的背景知识，让答案看起来更全面
让模型对每个块都逐字复述，一个字都不许改写
options_en: Give no constraining instructions at all and let the model answer freely from its own knowledge.
Grounding instructions: answer only from the context and cite a chunk ID per claim.
Instruct the model to freely add background knowledge beyond the provided context so answers look more complete.
Make the model recite every chunk word for word with no paraphrasing.
optionExplanations: 自由发挥没有约束，模型会编造上下文里没有的内容，忠实度和可追溯性全丢。
对；明确的 grounding + 引用要求 + 拒答示例把忠实度写进 prompt，是 prompt 级护栏的核心。
鼓励补充上下文外知识正好相反，会放大幻觉风险，违背 grounding 目标。
逐字复述不是作答，无法综合多块回答问题，也不解决忠实度约束。
optionExplanations_en: Free generation is unconstrained, so the model fabricates content not in the context, losing faithfulness and traceability.
Correct — explicit grounding plus citation requirements and refusal examples bake faithfulness into the prompt, the core prompt-level guardrail.
Encouraging outside knowledge is the opposite, amplifying hallucination and violating grounding.
Verbatim recitation isn't answering, can't synthesize across chunks, and doesn't address the faithfulness constraint.

termDefinitions.meaning: 要求模型只依据给定上下文作答、并标注来源，减少编造。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Grounding requires the model to answer only from the given context and cite sources, reducing fabrication.

scenario: 模型给了一个带引用的答案，但你担心它「挂着引用却其实没被那个块支持」的幻觉。
scenario_en: The model returns a cited answer, but you worry about hallucinations that cite a chunk that doesn't actually support the claim.
q: 生成后这一层最关键的核验做什么？
q_en: What is the key check in the post-generation layer?
why: 做引用核验：逐条检查每个被引用的块是否真的支持对应结论；若不支持，就用更严格的 prompt 重新生成，或直接返回「无法回答」。这把「假装有依据」的幻觉挡在输出之前，是生成后层的核心。
why_en: Citation verification: check whether each cited chunk actually supports its claim, and if not, regenerate with a stricter prompt or return 'cannot answer,' blocking fake-grounded hallucinations before output — the core of the post-generation layer.
tradeoff: 引用核验(挡住假引用幻觉但增加一轮开销/可能拒答) vs 直接输出(快但放过挂假引用的幻觉)
whenOtherWins: 若是低风险、非合规场景且延迟极敏感，可放宽核验、只抽查，换更低延迟。
options: 统计答案的长度和句子数，一旦超过阈值就直接截断
引用核验：查被引块是否真支持结论，不支持就重生成
把答案翻译成英文再翻回来，检查语法是否通顺
只要模型标了引用就默认可信，直接输出给用户
options_en: Count the answer's length and sentence count, and truncate the moment it exceeds a threshold.
Citation verification: check whether each cited chunk really supports the claim, else regenerate.
Translate the answer to English and back to check that the grammar reads well.
Trust any answer that carries a citation and hand it straight to the user.
optionExplanations: 长度和是否幻觉无关，截断改不了「引用挂假」的问题。
对；核验每条引用是否被块真正支持，是挡住假接地幻觉、守住忠实度的关键一步。
翻译查语法与引用真假无关，答不到忠实度核验。
标了引用不等于引用为真，正是幻觉常见形态，不能默认可信。
optionExplanations_en: Length is unrelated to hallucination; truncation doesn't fix a fake citation.
Correct — verifying each citation is truly supported by its chunk is the key step blocking fake-grounded hallucination and preserving faithfulness.
Grammar-checking via translation is unrelated to citation truthfulness and misses the verification.
A present citation isn't a true one — that's exactly a common hallucination — so it can't be trusted by default.

termDefinitions.meaning: 逐条检查被引用的块是否真的支持对应结论，不支持则重生成或拒答。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Citation verification checks whether each cited chunk truly supports its claim, regenerating or refusing if not.

termDefinitions.meaning: 判断一段文本是否在逻辑上支持另一句话，用来自动化检测幻觉。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An entailment model judges whether one text logically supports a statement, used to automate hallucination detection.

scenario: 生成后这一层要在答案返回用户之前，最后把一遍质量与安全关。
scenario_en: The post-generation layer is the final quality and safety gate before the answer reaches the user.
q: 生成后(post-generation)护栏包含哪些检查？(多选)
q_en: Which checks make up post-generation guardrails? (multiple)
why: 生成后三招都在输出前做：引用核验(每条引用是否被块支持，不支持就重生成或拒答)、内容安全/毒性扫描(挡有害输出)、用蕴含模型做幻觉检测(答案是否被上下文蕴含)。PII 脱敏是生成前的事，不在这一层。
why_en: All three run before output: citation verification (is each citation supported, else regenerate or refuse), a content-safety/toxicity scan (block harmful output), and hallucination detection via an entailment model (is the answer entailed by the context). PII redaction is a pre-generation concern, not this layer.
options: 引用核验：每条引用是否被块真正支持，不支持就重生成或返回无法回答
内容安全/毒性分类器扫描，挡住有害输出
用蕴含模型做幻觉检测，判断答案是否被上下文支持
PII 检测与脱敏，防个人信息进入 prompt
options_en: Citation verification: is each citation truly supported, else regenerate or return cannot-answer.
A content-safety/toxicity classifier scan to block harmful output.
Hallucination detection via an entailment model checking if the answer is supported by the context.
PII detection and redaction to keep personal info out of the prompt.
optionExplanations: 对；引用核验挡住「挂假引用」的幻觉，把不被支持的结论拦在输出前。
对；毒性扫描挡住有害/不当内容外发，是面向用户前的安全闸门。
对；蕴含模型自动判断答案是否被上下文支持，规模化地兜住幻觉。
错；PII 脱敏是块进 prompt 之前的生成前措施，不属于生成后层。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — citation verification blocks fake-citation hallucination, stopping unsupported claims before output.
Correct — a toxicity scan blocks harmful/inappropriate content from going out, the safety gate before the user.
Correct — an entailment model auto-judges whether the answer is context-supported, catching hallucination at scale.
Incorrect — PII redaction is a pre-generation measure before chunks enter the prompt, not the post-gen layer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用分类器检查输出是否含有害/不当内容，输出前拦下。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A toxicity scan uses a classifier to check output for harmful/inappropriate content and block it before release.

scenario: 护栏阈值设太严，很多合法问题被拒答；设太松，又可能放过有害或越权的输出。
scenario_en: Set guardrail thresholds too strict and many legitimate queries get refused; too permissive and harmful or over-permission output slips through.
q: 护栏阈值该怎么定，两端各有什么代价？
q_en: How should guardrail thresholds be set, and what's the cost at each extreme?
why: 两端都有代价：太严→合法请求被大量拒答、可用性差；太松→有害/越权输出漏出、合规风险。没有普适的点，要用领域专属评估数据校准阈值，在拒答率和风险之间找本领域可接受的平衡。
why_en: Both extremes cost: too strict → many legitimate requests refused, poor usability; too permissive → harmful/over-permission output leaks, compliance risk; there's no universal point, so calibrate thresholds with domain-specific eval data to balance refusal rate against risk for this domain.
tradeoff: 阈值严(少漏有害但多误拒合法) vs 阈值松(少误拒但多漏有害)
options: 阈值越严越好，宁可全部拒答也不能出一次错
太严→误拒合法请求；太松→漏出有害输出；用领域数据校准
阈值越松越好，尽量别打扰用户的正常提问
存在一个全行业通用的最佳阈值，直接照抄别人的配置即可
options_en: Stricter is always better — refuse everything rather than make one mistake.
Too strict wrongly refuses legitimate requests; too loose leaks harmful output; calibrate on domain data.
More permissive is always better — try not to interrupt users asking normal questions.
There's one industry-wide best threshold, so just copy someone else's configuration.
optionExplanations: 全拒虽不出有害内容，但可用性归零，产品没法用，不是可接受的一端。
对；严松各有代价，只能靠领域评估数据校准，在误拒和漏危险之间找本领域的平衡点。
一味放松会漏出有害/越权输出，合规风险不可接受。
不同领域(法务/医疗/客服)的风险容忍度不同，没有可照抄的通用阈值。
optionExplanations_en: Refusing all avoids harmful content but zeroes usability, making the product unusable — not an acceptable extreme.
Correct — strict and permissive each cost, so only domain eval data can calibrate the balance between wrong refusals and leaked risk.
Blind permissiveness leaks harmful/over-permission output, an unacceptable compliance risk.
Different domains (legal/medical/support) have different risk tolerance, so there's no copyable universal threshold.

termDefinitions.term: domain eval data / 领域评估数据
termDefinitions.meaning: 本领域标注好的测试样例，用来校准护栏阈值在拒答率和风险间的平衡。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Domain eval data is labeled test cases for the domain, used to calibrate guardrail thresholds between refusal rate and risk.

codeSample:
# 用领域标注集扫阈值，看两端代价怎么换
for t in 0.5 0.6 0.7 0.8 0.9; do
  python eval_guardrail.py --threshold "$t" \
    --dataset domain_eval.jsonl        # 本领域人工标注的合法/有害样例
  # 输出: false_refusal_rate(误拒合法) / leak_rate(漏出有害)
done
# 选点规则: 在 leak_rate <= 合规上限的前提下, 取 false_refusal_rate 最小的 t

scenario: 问题是「把 Q3 董事会备忘录里的政策变化，应用到 CRM 导出的客户名单上，估算收入影响」——答案要跨多个来源逐步拼出来。
scenario_en: The query is 'estimate the revenue impact of the Q3 board-memo policy change applied to the CRM-exported client list' — the answer must be chained across multiple sources.
q: 这种需要跨源多跳推理的问题，单趟 RAG 为什么不够，该怎么办？
q_en: Why does single-pass RAG fail on this multi-hop cross-source query, and what do you do?
why: 单趟 RAG(检索一次、生成一次)拿不到分散在多来源、且互相依赖的证据。改用 agentic RAG：让 orchestrator 迭代式检索——先拆子问题、各自跑完整检索+重排、评估凑齐没有、不够再精化重查，最后汇总生成。
why_en: Single-pass RAG (retrieve once, generate once) can't gather interdependent evidence spread across sources, so use agentic RAG: an orchestrator retrieves iteratively — decompose into sub-questions, run the full pipeline per sub-question, assess sufficiency, refine and re-retrieve if short, then assemble and generate.
tradeoff: agentic 多跳(跨源拼答质量高但多轮更慢更贵) vs 单趟(快省但答不了多跳依赖问题)
whenOtherWins: 若问题是单跳、一次检索就能覆盖(如「这条条款怎么写的」)，单趟 RAG 更快更省，agentic 是过度设计。
options: 把上下文窗口调到最大，一次性把所有相关来源全部塞进去，让模型自己去找
用 agentic RAG：拆子问题→分别检索→评估充分性→不足再重查
换一个更大的 LLM，让它一次生成就把多跳都想明白
多跑几次同样的单趟 RAG，对结果取多数投票
options_en: Max out the context window, stuff every single relevant source in at once, and let the model go find the links itself.
Use agentic RAG: decompose sub-questions → retrieve each → assess sufficiency → re-retrieve if short.
Switch to a bigger LLM and let it reason through all the hops in one generation.
Run the same single-pass RAG several times and majority-vote the results.
optionExplanations: 塞满窗口既触发中间迷失，也解决不了「先查到 A 才知道该查 B」的依赖关系，多跳仍断。
对；orchestrator 把大问题拆成子问题逐步检索、评估、精化，正是跨源多跳的正解。
更大的 LLM 补不了缺失的证据——多跳缺的是检索到的事实，不是推理能力。
重复单趟仍是各自独立检索，投票也拼不出需要跨源串联的答案。
optionExplanations_en: Stuffing the window triggers lost-in-the-middle and doesn't resolve the 'find A before knowing to query B' dependency, so multi-hop still breaks.
Correct — the orchestrator decomposes into sub-questions and iterates retrieve/assess/refine, the right answer for cross-source multi-hop.
A bigger LLM can't supply missing evidence — multi-hop lacks retrieved facts, not reasoning power.
Repeated single-pass still retrieves independently, and voting can't assemble an answer needing cross-source chaining.

termDefinitions.meaning: 由 orchestrator 编排多轮检索-评估-精化的 RAG，用于跨源多跳问题。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Agentic RAG has an orchestrator coordinate multiple rounds of retrieve-assess-refine, for multi-hop cross-source queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 答案需要串联多个来源、一步的结果决定下一步查什么。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Multi-hop means the answer chains across sources, where one step's result decides what to retrieve next.

scenario: agentic RAG 的 orchestrator 要把一个复杂多跳问题处理成最终答案。
scenario_en: The agentic RAG orchestrator turns a complex multi-hop query into a final answer.
q: 把 agentic RAG orchestrator 的处理步骤排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the agentic RAG orchestrator's steps correctly:
steps: 评估充分性：合起来的上下文够不够回答原问题
把原问题拆成若干独立子问题
每个子问题各自跑完整的检索+重排
不够则生成精化子查询、再检索一轮
带上全部护栏做最终汇总与生成
why: 先拆子问题→各自跑完整检索+重排→评估凑齐的上下文够不够→不够就精化子查询再检索一轮→够了带全部护栏汇总生成。评估-精化构成一个回路，直到充分或触达迭代上限。
why_en: Decompose into sub-questions → run full retrieval+reranking per sub-question → assess whether the combined context suffices → if not, refine sub-queries and retrieve again → once sufficient, assemble and generate with all guardrails; assess-refine forms a loop until sufficient or the iteration cap is hit.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  D["拆子问题"] --> R["各自检索+重排"] --> A{"充分?"}
  A -->|不够| Rf["精化子查询"] --> R
  A -->|够| G["带护栏汇总生成"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个复杂多跳问题拆成若干可独立检索的子问题。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Query decomposition breaks a complex multi-hop question into independently retrievable sub-questions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 判断已检索到的上下文是否足以回答原问题，不足则再检索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sufficiency assessment judges whether the retrieved context can answer the original question, retrieving again if not.

scenario: agentic RAG 每多一轮循环，大约就多一次检索延迟 + 一次 LLM 调用，成本和延迟随轮数线性增长。
scenario_en: Each agentic RAG loop adds roughly one retrieval latency plus one LLM call, so cost and latency grow linearly with rounds.
q: 「每轮≈一次检索+一次 LLM 调用」这个量级对设计意味着什么？
q_en: What does 'each loop ≈ one retrieval + one LLM call' imply for design?
why: 循环成本随轮数线性叠加，最坏情况可能无限循环。所以要给最大迭代次数封顶：用轮数上限把最坏延迟/成本框住，达上限还不充分就返回当前最好答案或「无法回答」，而不是无限查下去。
why_en: Loop cost stacks linearly with rounds and could loop unboundedly, so cap the max iterations: an iteration limit bounds worst-case latency/cost, and on hitting it you return the best answer so far or 'cannot answer' rather than looping forever.
options: 给迭代次数封顶：每轮线性叠加一次检索+调用，框住最坏延迟成本
轮数越多越好，应该一直循环下去直到答案打磨到完美为止
每轮的检索和调用成本始终固定不变，跟轮数没关系，完全不用封顶
这只是一个要死记硬背的数字，本身没有任何设计含义
options_en: Cap the iteration count: each loop stacks one retrieval plus one call linearly, bounding worst-case latency and cost.
More rounds are always better; keep looping until the answer is perfectly polished.
Each round's retrieval and call cost stays fixed no matter how many rounds run, so no cap is ever needed.
It is just a number to memorize by rote, with no design meaning of its own.

termDefinitions.meaning: 限制 agentic 循环的最大轮数，用来给最坏延迟和成本封顶。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An iteration cap limits the maximum agentic loop rounds to bound worst-case latency and cost.

optionExplanations: 对，每轮成本线性叠加，不封顶最坏情况会一直烧下去。
误解：一直循环到完美既没有终止条件，也会让延迟和成本失控。
误解：每轮都要多跑一次检索加一次调用，成本正随轮数往上叠加。
误解：这不是要背的数字，它决定了最坏情况下要花多少延迟和成本。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — per-round cost stacks linearly, and without a cap the worst case keeps burning resources forever.
Misconception: looping until perfect has no stopping condition and lets latency and cost spiral.
Misconception: every round adds one more retrieval and one more call, so cost does climb with rounds.
Misconception: it's not a number to memorize — it decides how much worst-case latency and cost you'll pay.

scenario: 面试官问什么时候用单趟 RAG、什么时候上 agentic RAG，想看你能否按问题复杂度选。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks when to use single-pass vs agentic RAG, checking whether you choose by query complexity.
q: 单趟 RAG 和 agentic RAG 在适用问题和成本上如何对比？
q_en: How do single-pass and agentic RAG contrast on fit and cost?
why: 单趟 RAG 一次检索一次生成，快而省，适合单跳问题；agentic RAG 多轮检索-评估-精化，慢而贵，但能答需要跨源串联的多跳复杂问题。取舍轴是「问题复杂度 vs 延迟/成本」，按问题选而非一刀切。
why_en: Single-pass RAG retrieves and generates once — fast and cheap, for single-hop queries; agentic RAG does multiple retrieve-assess-refine rounds — slower and costlier but answers multi-hop cross-source queries; the axis is query complexity vs latency/cost, chosen per query not one-size-fits-all.
tradeoff: 单趟(快省但只能单跳) vs agentic(能多跳但多轮更慢更贵)
options: 两者其实一样，任何问题都该用 agentic 更保险
单趟快而省适合单跳；agentic 慢而贵但能答多跳
单趟适合多跳、agentic 适合单跳，正好相反
agentic 更快更省成本，应该全面替代单趟 RAG
options_en: They are basically the same; use agentic for every question to be safe.
Single-pass is fast and cheap for single-hop; agentic is slow and costly but handles multi-hop.
Single-pass suits multi-hop and agentic suits single-hop — the other way around.
Agentic is faster and cheaper, so it should replace single-pass everywhere.
optionExplanations: 简单单跳问题用 agentic 是白白多花多轮延迟和 LLM 调用，过度设计。
对；按问题复杂度选——单跳走单趟省成本、多跳才上 agentic，取舍在复杂度与延迟/成本之间。
说反了：单趟只能单跳、agentic 才能多跳。
agentic 因多轮而更慢更贵，不可能全面替代更省的单趟。
optionExplanations_en: Using agentic on a simple single-hop query wastes extra rounds of latency and LLM calls — over-engineering.
Correct — choose by complexity: single-hop uses single-pass to save cost, multi-hop needs agentic, trading complexity against latency/cost.
Backwards: single-pass handles only single-hop and agentic handles multi-hop.
